The category took off during Covid and now shoppers are shelling out for high end brands like Fishwife. Today's guest Becca Millstein started the company in 2020, positioning it as a distinct, artisanal product, more akin to one might find in European grocery stores. In addition to the sheer challenges of scaling, the nature of the business itself has changed, influenced by climate change and geopolitics (shortages have led Morocco to suspend frozen sardine exports for instance). summary:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. 

On today's show, Iran wants to bar US and Israeli ships from crossing the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian media reports on a proposed deal being discussed by Iran and Oman. The semi-official Fars news agency says Iran also wants hostile countries to pay to be allowed to sail through the strait. European natural gas jumped following those reports.

Bond yields rose as the uncertainty in the Middle East raised inflation expectations. Traders now await the US jobs report for clues on the path ahead for interest rates.

Plus, the CEO of Rheinmetall has hit out at the German government over its decision to scrap a €10 billion naval contract. Germany's biggest defense company cut its sales forecast after losing the deal.

Today's guest: Madeleine Ronner, DWS, Senior Global Equities Portfolio Manager (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Houthis Carry Out Deadly Attack in Yemen and Hit Saudi Territory
title_cn: 胡塞武装在也门发动致命袭击并袭击沙特领土
summary: The Houthis conducted a “large-scale” attack against forces from Yemen’s Saudi-backed government, and struck the southwestern Saudi region of Najran, raising concerns over a widening of the US-Israeli war on Iran into a broader conflict.

title: Affordability is Top Issue for Midterms: Rep. Clark
title_cn: 负担能力是中期选举的首要问题：众议员克拉克
summary: House Minority Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA) says progressive Abdul Ed-Sayed's win in Michigan is a signal that voters are looking for "fighters" who will stand up for them in Congress. She says she believes Democrats will have the majority in the House come November, while signaling openness to a stopgap bill to avert a shutdown, noting that the Senate's proposal is a "big improvement." She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Sen. Cramer: Funding Vote Is Senate’s Top Priority
title_cn: 克莱默参议员：资助投票是参议院的首要任务
summary: With just one day left in the Senate’s session before a scheduled August recess, Republican Senator Kevin Cramer of North Dakota says lawmakers’ first priority is passing a continuing resolution to fund the government through December 11. On Republican holdouts over Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general, Cramer says he is hopeful President Donald Trump could weigh in and persuade them to support his nominee. He also says regular conversations between Trump and Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh are appropriate, noting it would be “strange” if they weren’t speaking somewhat regularly, as long as the central bank remains independent. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
